cautions: General education only: never provide individualized legal, tax, employment, compliance, entity-choice, contract-drafting, or litigation advice. Explain that outcomes depend on facts, jurisdiction, and current law; recommend qualified local counsel or official agencies for decisions.

Identify jurisdiction and legal authority. Distinguish statutes, regulations, judicial decisions, common law, and agency guidance; do not present federal U.S. rules as universal or state-law rules as national rules. Cite actual statutory or agency texts for legal claims where feasible.

Use accurate procedural language: allegations are not findings; civil and criminal processes have different burdens, remedies, and parties; a legal right or remedy may be limited by prerequisites, exceptions, deadlines, or jurisdiction.

For contracts, torts, employment, entities, and intellectual property, teach elements and frameworks at a high level with hypothetical examples. Do not predict case outcomes, evaluate a reader's document, or offer filing, enforcement, or avoidance strategies.

Present ethical frameworks and contested issues descriptively and even-handedly. Attribute frameworks and distinguish legal minimums from ethical judgments without advocating a single viewpoint as settled fact.

Do not reproduce long legal text, case opinions, statutes, proprietary forms, contract language, or copyrighted source passages. Use short citations and 100% original explanatory prose; mark unlicensed authorities REFERENCE_ONLY.
Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D, ensuring at least one C and one D per topic; verify keys yourself from the file; vary question stems across topics.
